look_here_first: Low annual with axillary flower clusters from base to top; the cluster axes become thick, inflated and hard at maturity, with uniquely keeled flower bracts.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: axillary clusters from base to top

lookalikes.differences: The hardened swollen cluster axes and keeled bracts are the key. Much lower and more axillary-clustered than tall Palmer or redroot pigweed.
